item.title: Evidence- and Rights-Governed Maintenance Learning: Why PUBLIC and HOLD Both Matter
item.description:
Problem: a fluent explanation is not necessarily a supported answer

Qualification material fragments questions, answers, theory, NCS units, and practical visuals across sources. AI can fill gaps fluently while still relying on:

  • conflicting answer candidates;
  • images without publication rights;
  • theory that is textually similar but semantically wrong;
  • answers already present in a pre-submit client payload;
  • one UI forced across written and practical answer formats.

The project goal is therefore not rapid question growth. It is a platform that publishes only evidence-qualified learning and preserves uncertainty as HOLD.

item.title: Fail-Closed AI Authority & Evidence Plane: Visibility Is Not Execution Authority
item.description:
Problem: test success is not execution authority

These statements describe different facts:

  • a model read data;
  • a model recommended an action;
  • local code passed tests;
  • an authorized person approved a bounded action;
  • the same artifact ran in the operating environment;
  • an external effect occurred and was read back.

Without that separation, “test PASS” can become “ready to deploy,” recommendation can become order approval, and local state can be mistaken for external effect.
